For each firm i and each year t in our sample, we compute earnings forecasts for up to five years into the future by multiplying the independent variables as of year t with the coefficients from the pooled regression estimated using the previous ten years of data.

scope.quote: In this paper, we propose a new approach to estimate the ICC. We use earnings forecasts generated by a cross-sectional model instead of analysts’ forecasts to proxy for cash flow expectations.

We estimate model-based earnings forecasts for up to five years into the future and then use those earnings forecasts to compute the ICC for more than 170,000 firm-year observations over the period 1968–2008.

method.quote: Specifically, for each year between 1968 and 2008, we estimate the following pooled cross-sectional regressions using the previous ten years of data:

sample.quote: Our sample includes all NYSE, Amex, and Nasdaq listed securities with sharecodes 10 or 11 (i.e., excluding ADRs, closed-end funds, and REITs) that are at the intersection of the CRSP monthly returns file from July 1963 to June 2009 and the Compustat fundamentals annual file from 1963 to 2009.

For each firm i and each year t in our sample, we compute earnings forecasts for up to five years into the future by multiplying the independent variables as of year t with the coefficients from the pooled regression estimated using the previous ten years of data.

review_notes: The source-selected baseline is the fitted Eq. (1) cross-sectional earnings forecast model because it is the new measurement input for the paper’s ICC approach. It is estimated for forecast horizons τ=1–5; Table 1 reports horizons 1–3 while the source says horizons 4–5 were estimated but available upon request.

Later forecast-performance/ERC comparisons and ICC return tests evaluate or apply the model outputs, and the five ICC valuation models are not fitted regressions; they are excluded from the retained baseline family.

The underlying pooled cross-sectional estimator remains unnamed, exact rolling training-fit Ns are not reported, and the earliest stated ten-year windows are unexplained against the stated 1963 data start.
